# South Dakota LRC — the reply we SENT, 2026-09-29

## STATUS: **SENT.** This is the record. Kept VERBATIM; do not edit the quoted text.

Sent by Cantrell from `chris@empowered.vote` to `LRC@sdlegislature.gov` at **12:51 PM on
2026-09-29**, one hour and fifty-two minutes after the Council's routing arrived. Supplied by the
operator 2026-09-30 from the Gmail thread.

🔴 **THE THREAD IS ANSWERED. Do not send another reply, and do not send the original request again.**
The original is [`2026-09-28-sd-legislature-portrait-permission.md`](./2026-09-28-sd-legislature-portrait-permission.md).

---

## 🔴🔴 THIS LETTER MADE A DECISION, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE DRAFTS ASSUMED

Read the first line. **"I'm comfortable not using any of their official pictures, and we won't."**

▶ **THE PER-MEMBER ROUTE WAS DECLINED, NOT TAKEN.** The Council said to ask each of the 105
legislators individually. The operator answered that we will not use the Legislature's portraits at
all. So:

- **There are NO member letters.** An earlier note in this directory called them "a separate, later
  artifact"; that is superseded. Nobody is writing to 105 members.
- **`photo_license` stays `unknown` on all 105 and nothing is imported from
  `lawmakerdocuments.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net`.** Not pending — settled.
- **The only path to a South Dakota portrait is a source that is not the Legislature's**, and the
  Ballotpedia trap still applies in full: Ballotpedia rehosts the Legislature's own studio
  portraits, including prior sessions', so "it is on Ballotpedia" does not make it usable. See
  `../sd-portrait-sources.md`.
- **Everyone else keeps the shrugging figure and the notice.** That is the finished state for them,
  not a waiting state.

⚠ **THE LETTER DESCRIBES OUR VOTER-FACING COPY TO A GOVERNMENT BODY**, so the copy has to keep
matching it: a placeholder, plus a note saying the Legislature reserves its portraits and that
permission rests with each member. If that copy is ever reworded, read this paragraph first — we
told the Council what it would say.

⚠ **IT ALSO STATES THE CHALLENGER ASYMMETRY TO THE COUNCIL**, in writing: challengers publish their
own photographs freely, so the practical effect of the reservation is that challengers appear with
a face and incumbents do not. That asymmetry was already a known programme hazard. It is now a
position we have put on the record with a legislature.

⚠ **AND IT STATES A PROGRAMME FACT**: South Dakota is the first body of all we have written to that
has not granted this centrally. Anyone repeating that claim should re-check it against the letters
in this directory first — it was true on 2026-09-29.

---

## The sent text, verbatim

```
Chris Cantrell <chris@empowered.vote>
Sep 29, 2026, 12:51 PM (19 hours ago)
to LRC

Sure - I'm comfortable not using any of their official pictures, and we won't.
 
Where a member's photograph exists somewhere other than the legislature's site, we'll use that.  Where it doesn't, that member's entry will carry a shrugging stick-figure placeholder and a short note saying the Legislature reserves its portraits and that permission rests with each member - so residents understand it wasn't our omission or mistake, but a choice made by SD's Legislative Research Council.

For what it's worth, this is the first body, of all I've written to, that hasn't granted this centrally.  Public figures tend to have photos they will share with the press for this very reason.  Since the candidates running against these members publish their own photographs freely, the practical effect is that challengers will appear with a face and incumbents won't.  I'm not sure how that supports your legislature or constituents, but we will comply.


Thanks for your assistance.
```

## What it replied to

```
On Tue, Sep 29, 2026, 10:59 AM LRC <lrc@sdlegislature.gov> wrote:
You will need to ask each legislator individually as they are the ones who can grant permission for use.
```

From the Council as a body. No named person, so **do not attribute it to an individual.**

🔴 **It is a ROUTING, not a REFUSAL**, and that reading still stands even though we declined the
route. The Council said it does not hold the right; the member does. "SD rejected us" and "SD has a
blanket policy against press use" are both more than they wrote.

## How this file came to exist late

The sent wording was missing from the repo for a day. On 2026-09-30 a session read the then-current
note — *"Operator was drafting a reply"* — found the session record cleared, concluded nothing had
gone out, and **drafted a replacement reply for a letter that had already been sent.** It was
presented for approval rather than sent, so nothing reached South Dakota. The draft has been
deleted; this file replaces it.

🔴 **"OPERATOR WAS DRAFTING X" IS A NOTE ABOUT A MOMENT, NOT A STATE.** It does not decay into
"X was never sent", and a cleared session is not evidence either way. **Ask before redoing outbound
correspondence.**

⚠ **AND A SENT LETTER MUST NOT BE RECONSTRUCTED FROM A HINT.** When the operator said the letter
"should start with 'sure'", that was a true fact about the sent text — but writing the file from it
would have invented a record of what a government body was told. The right answer was to wait for
the actual text, which is what is above.
